summary.text: Aaron Bean is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 4th District, first elected in 2022. Before Congress he was a community bank president and small-business founder, mayor of Fernandina Beach, and a Florida state representative and senator. He is seeking a third term and sits on the House Ways and Means Committee.

paragraphs.text: Bean was born in Fernandina Beach, Florida, in 1967. According to his congressional website, he grew up as the youngest of nine children in a working-class family, the grandson of a coal miner and the son of teachers.
He graduated from high school in 1985 and earned a B.S. in finance from Jacksonville University in 1989.

Bean worked as an auctioneer and as a relationship development officer with UF Health Jacksonville, and his congressional website says he was a community bank president and built four small businesses, including the High Energy Auction Company.
Bean began in public office as a city commissioner and then mayor of his hometown of Fernandina Beach, serving from 1996 to 1999.

He served in the Florida House of Representatives from 2000 to 2008 and the Florida Senate from 2012 to 2022; in the Senate he was President Pro Tempore and chaired the Appropriations Subcommittee on Health and Human Services, according to his congressional website.
Bean won the open U.S. House seat in 2022 with 60.5% of the vote over Democrat LaShonda Holloway, succeeding John Rutherford, and took office on January 3, 2023; he was re-elected in 2024.

During the 118th Congress (2023-2024), Bean chaired the Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education subcommittee of the Committee on Education and the Workforce and served on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business. In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he sits on the Committee on Ways and Means, including its Subcommittees on Social Security, Work and Welfare, and Oversight.
He describes himself as the founder and co-chair of the Delivering Outstanding Government Efficiency (DOGE) Caucus, which he says works to reduce government fraud, waste, and abuse.
According to his congressional website, Bean and his wife, Abby, have three sons and a granddaughter born in 2024.
